lines.text: What if all the ants disappeared?
Vik bets his whole picnic on it.
But there are about twenty quadrillion ants on Earth, and together they outweigh every wild bird and mammal combined.
That's about two and a half million for every person.
So when they vanish, everything they were carrying just… drops.
Ants are the planet's cleanup crew. Without them, fallen fruit, dead leaves and bugs pile up and rot right where they land.
Then the ground changes. Ant tunnels let air and water into the soil, and without them, it packs down hard.
The one full of tunnels drinks the water straight down to the roots. The packed one? It just spills over.
And the seeds? Many plants rely on ants to carry their seeds underground. Now they just lie there.
So forests start to thin, one missing tiny worker at a time.
And Vik's picnic? Buried under rotting leaves. Turns out he'd miss them after all.
So next time you step on one, ask yourself…
